applicability: any non-negative integer — the rule is universal because 100 is a multiple of 4, so n mod 4 depends only on the last two digits of n

operand_draw.rationale: Draw one three-digit integer. The presentation filter only pins the rendered width (three digits fits the working line at 60 px without wrapping); it encodes no property of divisibility, so the trick is tested on whatever the seed produces.

nulls.reason: The last-two-digits rule for 4 has no exception on the integers. Because 100 = 25 × 4, every n satisfies n ≡ (n mod 100) (mod 4), so 4 divides n iff 4 divides the two-digit block. The generator check confirms this equivalence exhaustively for n in [0, 10000], and the Verifier is expected to widen or re-derive it.
